priorIssues.issue: w26b-1 (medium) diamond pan a field of big light stars
priorIssues.evidence: q15 s3 pan: bright 0.034 vs y_47300 0.088 (w26 0.214), p90/50 1.15 vs 1.37 (w26 1.72), blobs 0.6 / kpx vs 14.9 - the lattice is now nearly gone - but L 106.9 vs 74.1 (w26 73.2) and B/R 1.65 vs 1.81. Cause: layer 34 at gain 0.45 multiplies base by mix(1, 0.4, 0.45) = 0.73 on average while photoBase still scales the colour x2.5 for a full-gain tile (mean 0.4), so the pan is ~1.8x too bright in linear. At thumbnail (z_pans.png, q15) the diamond pan is now the lightest, lavender-periwinkle slab in the row, where in y_47300 it is the darkest pan with a faint ghost lattice.

issues.title: Diamond pan overshot: now the lightest pan (L107 vs 74), lattice almost gone
issues.evidence: q15 s3 pan L106.9 vs y_47300 74.1 (w26 73.2), B/R 1.65 vs 1.81, p90/50 1.15 vs 1.37, bright 0.034 vs 0.088 (z_pans.png). The shader multiplies base by mix(1, 2c, gain); the y_diamond tile is stored at ENC 5 (2c mean ~0.4) and photoBase scales the colour x2.5 assuming full gain, so at gain 0.45 the mean multiplier is 0.73 instead of 0.4: ~1.8x too bright in linear, and the relative contrast falls to ~0.25 of the full tile where ~0.5 is wanted. It is the most visible mismatch in q15 at thumbnail size.
issues.fix: 03_tex.js (shared one-liners): PHOTO_GAIN[34] and LAYER_PARAMS[34][2] 0.45 -> 0.7 (relative star contrast 0.4g/(1-0.6g) = 0.48 of full -> p90/50 ~1.35). 09a_econ.js l.50 ECON_PAN_B colour '#4e5676' -> ~'#39415e' (linear x0.56 for the higher mean multiplier 0.58/0.73 and the L target, red x0.92 / blue x1.10 for B/R). Cleaner alternative: give photoBase a gain argument (k = 1 / mix(1, 0.4, gain) style) so the colour is gain-independent. Targets q15 s3: L 70-78, B/R 1.75-1.85, p90/50 1.32-1.42, bright 0.07-0.11, blob p90 <= 25 px; the pan must read as the darkest of the four as in y_47300.
